name: Maritime Oil Painting
description: Oil-painting look for covers and hero scenes — loose visible brushwork, a pale ivory tonal range left open as negative space, and sepia, ochre and gold weathered colour against deep shadow.
style_bible: Nineteenth-century oil painting on primed canvas. Medium and surface: loose visible brushwork, oil laid in directional strokes that stay readable as paint, thin scumbled glazes in the open upper field and thicker impasto reserved for edges that catch the light, with fine craquelure and a warm varnish bloom over the whole surface. Edges and shapes: painterly and soft almost everywhere, larger forms held together by tone rather than outline, fine linear details suggested with a few dry-brushed hairlines rather than drawn thread by thread, horizon slightly broken and never ruler-straight. Palette: sepia, ochre, raw and burnt sienna, aged gold and warm ivory through the sky, moving to deep navy, slate green and cold grey in the shadow, with oxblood and a single muted vermilion reserved for the smallest accents. Lighting: soft diffused daylight from a low overcast sun, light entering from one side and passing through cloud rather than striking hard; luminous sky, no hard modern key light, no rim light, no artificial glow. Texture: canvas tooth visible through thin passages, dry-brush drag on fine linear forms, granular particles, and broken edges with light behind them. Subject grammar: one clear focal subject held against a low horizon and a wide open upper field. Where a figure appears, it is anonymous and never a recognisable individual. Framing: hold the upper third to two-fifths pale, open and largely empty as deliberate negative space; place the subject low and to one side on a clear diagonal, keep the horizon below centre, and let atmosphere rather than detail carry the distance. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed subject, place, era detail, event, or copied composition.
